findings: Both views describe a Singapore customer with a participating bank or non-bank app authorizing a Stripe PayNow QR payment in SGD for a Singapore account. Payment confirmation follows completed authorization, Stripe balance availability follows one day later, and bank payout follows the account schedule.

November documents instant provisional access, domestic coverage, 0.50–200,000 SGD, and a product/feature matrix. It explicitly identifies single-use and unsupported setup, off-session and capture flows. Billing's send_invoice collection is compatible with checkout of an invoice, while automatic invoice charge is unsupported.

November gives the pending refund state, up-to-five-minute processing, no cancellation, Dashboard/Refund API status inspection and signed webhook notification. Failed refunds restore the Stripe balance and require a different refund method.

The buyer can scan from a different device or save and upload the code on the same device. Authorization expires in one hour, at which point the merchant's integration can use an event to bring the buyer back and create a new PaymentIntent and QR. A previously successful QR is rejected.

Connect retains all three charge types and capability/MCC prerequisites. Charge type controls the merchant of record and displayed merchant name. Bank statement fields and generated PayNow reference are separate from Connect merchant presentation.
substantive_changes: Replace permanent 1.3% with May 2026 dated evidence; November links pricing without quoting a rate.
Add November’s provisional access, same-country scope and 0.50–200,000 SGD limits, plus explicit setup/off-session and capture capability qualifications.

Separate next-day Stripe balance availability from bank payout scheduling. Document terminal public preview and retained manual listing, and separate refund status from notification event with the 90-day method ceiling.
Add QR same-device route, repeat-attempt qualification, and merchant display/reference surfaces while preserving the substance of earlier fixed descriptor and chargeback limits.
historical_claims_to_preserve: May 2026 explicitly quotes 1.3%, documents T+1 Stripe balance availability by default with distinct daily versus weekly payout examples, and describes no standard chargeback or dispute balance debit.

May 2026 documents manual Terminal listing, 90-day full/partial asynchronous refunds and failed-fund return, one-hour QR expiry, no descriptor customization and the Connect capability and MCC requirements.

May 2026 describes the merchant of record as determining which Stripe account can create a payment with a particular PaymentMethod. Keep that statement dated separately from November's charge-type-dependent merchant name and merchant-of-record guidance.
conflicts: Source and Stripe index use T+1 payout shorthand. Both dated raws distinguish balance availability from scheduled bank payout.
Source and concept present 1.3% as an active price. The November raw supplies a pricing link only.

Source and concept assert that QR authentication prevents chargebacks. Stripe attributes low fraud risk to separate app authentication and documents that PayNow has no standard dispute/chargeback flow.

The overview marks Payment Element supported, while the May companion acceptance summary says no Elements path. The overview supports qualifying the concept by scope, while the November acceptance implementation requires evidence from its own capture.

New raw `raw/stripe-payments-paynow-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw `raw/stripe-paynow-2025.md`. Current summaries `wiki/sources/source-stripe-paynow.md`.

- Q1. For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/paynow`, what documented behavior, prerequisites, actors and state transitions does the complete new capture establish? How do these compare with the matched prior capture and each mapped summary?

reviewed_answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/paynow, source-stripe-paynow.md covers Singapore sellers accepting SGD QR payments from Singapore customers using a participating bank or non-bank app. In old raw lines 8–35 and 59–87 and new raw lines 9–20 and 163–199, the buyer must authorize in the app within one hour, Stripe confirms completion immediately, and an expired session needs a new PaymentIntent and QR after the customer is brought back. November makes same-device saving/upload and provisional access explicit. Both dates distinguish confirmation from next-day balance availability and later scheduled payout. Old raw lines 97–101 and new raw lines 85–99 support the 90-day ceiling and alternate refund method after failure. November adds pending status, processing up to five minutes and no cancellation. New raw lines 136–161 retain send_invoice, manual Terminal listing and Connect prerequisites, and explicitly date Terminal public-preview support.
reviewed_answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/paynow, source-stripe-paynow.md requires updates beyond the template and matrix: old raw lines 54–56 quoted 1.3% in May, while new raw lines 9–20 link price and retain scheduled payout after one-day balance availability (old raw lines 123–127). New raw lines 52–57 and 85–103 supply transaction limits, refund-state and dispute qualifications. New raw lines 105–161 distinguish product support, single-use limitations, Terminal preview and the charge-type-dependent Connect presentation. Keep fixed statement/reference details distinct from Connect merchant display under new raw lines 201–207. Update wiki/stripe-index.md and the PayNow section and source-list entry in wiki/concepts/stripe-real-time-payments.md, and add the reciprocal concept link from the source. The companion May guide describes only its captured Checkout/direct procedures. Product-level Payment Element support does not establish the detail of a separate acceptance variant.
